title: An arrow sources a bond id that does not exist in the from state, on a species that has no bonds at all

expect.note: Adversary pass, Phase 1, attack surface 1. Rule source_bond_not_in_state had no negative control anywhere in the corpus. A lone sodium cation sits alone in the from state, with no bonds. The arrow claims a bond source with bondId "phantom-bond", which resolves against no species here, and sinks it as a lone pair landing on the real atom Na1. The to state is byte identical to the from state, following the same isolation pattern as the sibling fixture for source_atom_not_in_state: arrow-legality never reads the to state, so a step that changes nothing is the cleanest way to isolate the resolution rule from every check that does read it. WHY BOTH CHECKS ARE NAMED, and only these two. arrow-legality's RESOLUTION rule fires source_bond_not_in_state directly and, because the source does not resolve, the code skips every later rule for this arrow, including density and adjacency, exactly as legality.ts documents: 'a broken reference rather than a chemistry error, and a silent zero here would hide it'. conservation-electron-flow's own resolution pass walks referencedBondIds(arrow), finds "phantom-bond" absent from knownBondIds, and reports the identical unresolved reference before ever attempting declaredDeltas, matching the documented unavoidable cascade in fixtures/README.md: 'Bond sources are resolved BEFORE calling declaredDeltas, which throws on a bond id it cannot find... the unresolved reference has already been recorded as a violation of this same check.' Mass, charge, and valence pass because the to state is identical to the from state and Na1 is self consistent (formal charge +1, zero lone pairs, zero bonds, derived charge 1 - 0 - 0 = 1, matching).
